name: Big Nerd Gaming
description:
My name is Westen, aka “The Big Nerd”. I count myself as incredibly fortunate in this life. I have an amazing wife, a beautiful daughter, and tons of amazing friends, many of whom I consider family.
And yet, one weird thing has always been missing for me. Despite video games being one of my main passions, I’ve never had anyone to really talk about them with, besides some of the really big releases. When I make Facebook or Twitter posts about gaming, I’m mostly talking to a digital wall.
The other thing missing from my life has been writing. Despite growing up only wanting to be a journalist, it never ended up working out for me. I often have an itch to write, which mostly ends up being long twitter threads on my personal account that a few people might actually click all the way through.
So, long story short, I’m hoping this blog is a way for me to find even a small gaming community, somewhere in this vast digital landscape we live in. And also, it’s a way to fire off the many hot gaming takes I have. It literally kills me to hold them inside. I’m dying, and I hope this blog can be the sweet release I desperately need.
Also, I’m literally addicted to ranking things, and it’ll be nice to have all those ranks in one spot when I need to reference them. It’s the little things, you know?
Thank you for checking this page out, and I hope you will follow me on Twitter, and interact when you can!

name: Cania's Blog
description:
Hi, I'm Cania!
Alright, now that we've got the basics out of the way, I guess it's time for a less broad description. I'm Cania! My name comes from a joke which you'll certainly discover if you dig deeply enough into this site. I'm non-binary, I'm married, and I live in the frigid north of the United States.

I'll be honest: my main interest is and always has been video games. When I was 3 or 4 my parents had to take away the NES because I got too into Punch-Out!! and started trying to destroy all of our furniture with my fists. When I was in 3rd grade I lent my friend my copy of Yoshi Story (with the manual) and when I got it back his dog had chewed up the manual and I was quite upset. I learned how to make DOOM maps in 2020, 27 years after it was released. My latest project was playing every Golf game on the Game Boy.

But recently I've tried to cultivate other interests - this site is one of them. I've started drawing, podcasting, making music, and collecting...stuffed NeoPets???

Jack of all trades, master of some - that's me!

Anyway, check out the various links at the top - I'll show you everything I've done, a bunch of things I'm interested in, and all the resources I used to build this very site. Have a good time!!!

name: Game Production Alchemist
description:
My name is Rob Sandberg, and I am the Game Production Alchemist! I started developing video games on my Apple II as a teenager in the 80s and have since been professionally making games and building game services for over thirty years. As a producer, I have shipped dozens of games from concept to live operations on mobile, console, PC, VR and web.

I am credited for award-winning AAA titles, top-grossing apps that have earned billions (yes, billions with a B) in revenue, games with big licensed brands, budget Walmat shovel-ware, some of the lowest-ranking games of all time, and so many cancelled games I have lost count. The good, the bad and the ugly, but every game was a learning experience. I wear my scars with pride. See my LinkedIn bio or Alchemy Society credentials below for more details. Here are many of the games that I had the privilege of being a part of.

I reside in Buckinghamshire, United Kingdom, in the shadow of the Chiltern Hills, writing in my secret laboratory in an undisclosed location. In the latter part of August each year, I can be found at the 10/7 Bar located at the Tokyo Ranger Outpost in Black Rock City, Nevada.

Game & Word’s content dives as deep as possible into the hobby we love, highlighting individual games’ connections to humanity and the world. History, culture, psychology, literature, and even philosophy can all shape the games we play and fondly remember.

By exploring these links, not only do we gain a greater appreciation for these games, we demonstrate that—far from being a childish time-waster—a good game can be as creative, powerful, and worthy of recognition as a good book, song, or movie. name: Museum of Screens
description:
About us
The Internet is a media in constant evolution, but not often in a good way. The rise of social media and big tech companies overshadowing smaller websites slowly turns the Internet into a predictable market, shaped to suit the needs of the peoples in charge. And they do very little to preserve the history of the Internet.
Sadly, browser games are often the first things to be lost. Sure many notable games are preserved and celebrated, but it’s only the tip of the iceberg. There are literally thousands of games out there, made by amateurs, small teams or companies. Passion projects that peoples poured their hearts into, got a bit of recognition but were lost because of various reasons. Even worse, some games got incredibly famous outside of the creator’s intent because they were copied and pasted on other websites, without any credits.
We can see many projects of preservation nowadays, but browser games are unique in the matter, because they are the least tangibles ones. Even downloadable-only games can be archived, but often, browser games are just available as long as the server they are running on is still operational. And sure, Flash files can be downloaded and archived, but what about online game in PHP?
I didn’t wanted to make a large scale project of game preservation, but I wanted to create something that could be used as a reference of browser games history, by collecting as much information as possible about them. And ost of all, I wanted to give proper credits to all these forgotten creators.

name: RetroRGB
description:
RetroRGB.com is a website with corresponding YouTube, Podcast and social media accounts dedicated to highlighting the people and projects in the retro gaming scene.  The main section of the website is a review and news blog, however we also feature interviews, modding guides and a weekly podcast that sums up everything that’s been going on in the scene.
Since “RetroRGB 3.0” launched as a blog, the website has taken on contributors from all over the world;  People with love and passion for retro games and hardware, who contribute their knowledge and experience to help spread the word of all the amazing projects out there.  Many of the contributions on RetroRGB are in the form of written posts and if you’d like to learn more about the writer, please click on their name in the heading to learn more about them.  Some people contribute solely as a hobby, while others create content for a living and rely on your support to continue.  Please check their bio’s to learn more about them and consider contributing, or even just spreading the word.
We’ll also try to find more ways to highlight the people working on behind-the-scenes projects as well, as their work is essential to keeping the site going and is often the most time-consuming.  Recognition for their work is often a shoutout in a video, or a mention in a post…but that’s not enough and we’ll get better at highlighting the community that keeps this all going!

name: Rewinder
description:
Rewinder is a UK-based independent publication focused on delivering video game related journalism.

Our goal is to provide timely, verified, knowledgeable coverage across news, reviews, features, and more. We're a team of three established journalists who've been in this space for years and have a wealth of experience. Henry's also Senior Editor at UploadVR with freelance bylines at Eurogamer, IGN, PC Gamer and more. Managing Editor Scott McCrae has freelance bylines with TechRadar, Daily Mirror, and GamesRadar+, while Deputy Editor Lex Luddy is EIC at startmenu.

name: Seasoned Gaming
description:
Passion for gaming is the foundation of everything we do here at Seasoned Gaming. Founded in 2015, this site has been built around the idea that gaming coverage deserves better than quick hits and clickbait leading to pages covered in ads.

So we went back to the basics and designed a gaming site with the sole focus of providing news on all platforms without any monetization or focus on what’s “hot.” Instead, we are a fully independent site whose staff is comprised of tech writers, engineers, application developers, and more, who simply have a long-term passion for gaming in all forms.

Our coverage is as unique and varied as our contributors, and we celebrate the diversity of opinion and individual perspectives people from all walks of life bring to games.

name: Sidequesting
description: SideQuesting is a website for gaming enthusiasts that bases itself not only on the games, but also the culture surrounding the players. The website will often feature more personal articles based on aspects of the industry that our staff, friends, and families experience.

My name is Dylan Cornelius, and I’ve been writing about video games for 14 years. Mostly on Questicle.net and SegaDoes.com, but also for sites that no longer exist.

Here at the Society, my goal is to cultivate a community dedicated to exploring and discussing the history of video games. We do this through personal stories, historical deep dives, expansive retrospectives, and even the occasional clickbait list. Whatever it takes!

Our focus is predominantly on retro games, but we will cover any modern game that strikes our fancy as well.

name: Super Phillip Central
description:
"Video games with a heroic touch!"

Greetings! I'm SuperPhillip, aka Phil,  I'm a gaymer on the spectrum--my very first game was Super Mario Bros. 2 (the U.S. version), and I've been gaming for almost all of my 38 years on this earth. I enjoy writing about games, creating my own games (or at least tinkering with game design and game making), composing music, watching my favorite TV shows and movies, and trying to break the stigma of mental illness.

name: Survival Horrors
description:
The main driving force behind this project is to create a definitive list of every survival horror game ever made. While other websites attempt to list survival horror games, they often include titles that don’t quite fit the genre or overlook key games, especially those from indie developers.

Initially, I also aimed to share upcoming survival horror games, but I quickly realized that documenting and researching upcoming titles is just as demanding as maintaining the list of existing games. Despite the challenge, my dedication to this genre keeps me motivated I am committed to continuously improving and expanding the upcoming games section, making it a valuable resource for survival horror fans.

I highly value feedback to help inform and refine my list. While we may never reach a consensus on what defines a survival horror game, my goal is to inform enthusiasts about the survival horror games they might have missed, particularly those from indie developers, and to promote and support upcoming indie games.

If you’d like to get in touch, the best way is to join our Discord group or connect with us on social media.

name: Sushiball Games
description:
We met at a comic book convention in late 2017 as Spider-Man and Supergirl, were engaged three months later and married later that year. We gravitate towards creative endeavors, and naturally, board games allowed us to find one more way we could spend time together. We love to spend time with our family and, of course, our little dog Sushi, all of which have helped us with our passion project.

Now we focus on reviewing games together, both published and Kickstarter stages. If you have any projects you’d like us to review, or have questions for us, feel free to reach out on our Contact page

The Platform Layer is a publication about gaming platforms as systems.

It examines Xbox, PlayStation, Nintendo, PC, and emerging platforms through a systems lens — focusing on strategy, ecosystem dynamics, and the business models that shape how we play.

Rather than reviews or news, the work here looks beneath hardware and headlines to understand incentives, access models, and structural decisions that drive behavior at scale.

name: The Solo Gamedev
description:
My name is Mariusz and I’m a big dreamer!

Among many things, I want to learn how to make video games and make them. Maybe not full-time, maybe not in a different company. My way, whatever it takes. I started this newsletter in 2021 (I think…) on Twitter’s Revue (R.I.P.). Now I’m here, on Substack, sharing what I learned, what help me make another step. Join me, and someday I will be able to tell you how to become a game developer, with a step-by-step action plan! Who knows, I might tell anyone how to achieve their goals ;-)

name: Thinky Games
description:
Welcome, puzzlers and problem solvers! We're a community of thinky fans who want to share amazing games with as many people as possible.

Thinky games are those you love to solve — all about careful reasoning, rather than fast reflexes or dexterity. If you find yourself thinking through a problem and then, when the insights finally dawn on you, exclaiming “aha!”, you’re probably playing a thinky game.

We believe thinky games are for everyone. If you enjoy relaxing with a crossword, figuring out whodunit before the TV detective does, or wrapping your head around an intriguing riddle, we think you'll love these games. Logic games, detective games, mystery games, strategy games, math games, adventure games — there are so many wonderful thinky games to discover!

Our hope, through sharing these games, is to introduce more people to the joys of playful problem solving.

name: Thrilling Tales of Old Video Games
description:
My name is Drew Mackie, and I have been writing about video games in one form or another ever since I had an internet connection
I’m down to write about anything that could be considered classic gaming, but my personal areas of interest are Nintendo, Capcom, and Square — and specifically in the 8-bit and 16-bit eras. I know *a lot* about Super Mario Bros. 2, so expect to see a lot about Super Mario Bros. 2. But as I keep making posts, I’m hoping to veer away from Nintendo and into a broader look at old video games.

name: Time Extension
description: While other sites out there are constantly looking to the future and the promise of the "next big thing", here at Time Extension we do the exact opposite – we're looking back into the past to uncover hidden gems, proclaim stone-cold classics and shed a light on the human stories behind some of our favourite games, companies and systems.

name: Timenerf
description: Timenerf is designed to help you make better use of your time and the content is written from the perspective of how easy a game is to fit into the busy life you live. There will be circumstances where the writer may recommend a game because it is just that freaking good and something you should make time for.

name: Updater
description: Updater is your destination newsletter for incisive gaming and tech coverage you can’t get anywhere else. It’s named after what some newsrooms no longer have the budget to do anymore: keep a story updated, revisit it follow-up after follow-up, and glean new insights each time. It’s why you’ll see many stories on Updater about the gaming industry’s largest companies as they surface back in the news time and again.

name: Uppercut
description: Uppercut is a games and media site devoted to punching up through high quality content that focuses on highlighting marginalised voices and great criticism. We aim to do this by not only having a diverse staff, but also by bringing on and spotlighting other voices that are often pushed to the margins in mainstream games and media sites.

name: Urban Protagonist
description: Urban Protagonist started as just a name in 2012, gradually growing into the cyberpunk character he is today. Emerging from the rugged underbelly of a futuristic Bay Area, Urban is a relentless challenger of corporate control. He embodies the fight for independence, the spirit of rebellion, and the determination to change the system from within, despite a world designed to suppress him. Through this character, I channel my creative energy into crafting stories and developing games that delve into the themes of freedom, resistance, and perseverance in a future that feels all too real.

name: Voletic
description:
I want Voletic to continue to be the kind of site that it has always been - completely independent and unbridled. Here I’ll give my raw opinions about the world of video games - but don’t let that deceive you.

Giving raw opinions is often a way for people to disguise that they really just want to be a bit nasty. That’s not my style. This is a nice place - where we can share and discuss gaming openly - and respect both the people that create them, and the audience that enjoys them. It’s an open opinion space - it just happens that I generally have quite nice opinions.
